solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Catch sight of son with trophy

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy won in sport

explanation.surface: A parent spots their son walking off with a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, a plain synonym for catching sight of it.

clue.text: Paint a picture of harbour and fish

parts.note: a port is a harbour for ships
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: An artist sets out to paint a harbour scene with fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict, whether in paint or in words.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Inside a health centre, there is a qualified nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to give them medical care, which is to treat them.

clue.text: Fellow bachelor, not carrying as much weight

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees like BA
something that weighs less is lighter

explanation.surface: A single man has slimmed down and now weighs less than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British terms for a man or chap, often used with mild disapproval.

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means turned upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill in a bar or restaurant

explanation.surface: A sports club's bill has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is the club used to strike the ball in cricket or baseball.

clue.text: Is priest evil in Asian capital?

parts.note: a lama is a Buddhist priest in Tibet
bad means evil or wicked

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cleric in an Asian city is wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan, in Asia.

parts.note: home means at home, in, as in 'is anyone home?'
a run is a series, as in a run of wins

explanation.surface: A baseball run scored in a series of games.
explanation.definitionFit: A home run is the big baseball hit that lets the batter circle all the bases to score.

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of letters spanning the next two words

explanation.surface: More competitors will be in the next race.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, which is what more means.

indicators.note: something poor is badly made, so the letters of the next word are put together in another order

explanation.surface: A needy relative has come over from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor relation' reads as a set phrase, but 'Poor' only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things coming from or belonging to Asia, the lands lying to the east.

definitions.meaning: in chess, the final win that traps the king on the board

explanation.surface: A partner suffers a loss at the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a companion or spouse, and checkmate is the board-game defeat shortened to one word.

clue.text: Common sense required to enclose right legal document

indicators.note: the first piece wraps round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: wit can mean practical good sense, as in 'have the wit to'

explanation.surface: A lawyer insists that sense is needed to cover a proper legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order issued by a court, so a legal document.

clue.text: Welsh barman I treated after onset of cold

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the opening letter
the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter of cold is used
letters treated are processed into a new form, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A barman cares for someone after they come down with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the anagram of BARMAN I behind C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambria is the old Latin name for Wales, so its adjective means Welsh.

parts.note: what someone says asking for a repeat of something not heard, which is literally an instruction to return

explanation.surface: Someone asks what they will get back in exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What?' is the plain sense; 'in return' points to the literal reading, coming back a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday request to repeat what was said, meaning 'Pardon?' or 'What?'

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for time
a fluid arrangement is not fixed, so the letters of messy can flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes an untidy procedure involving liquid and the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' turns MESSY into SYSEM, and 'about' wraps that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or procedure, which is what a process is.

clue.text: Hybrid fruit beginning to grow in adapted lean-to

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the rearranged letters
adapted means altered, so the letters of lean-to are reshaped
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gardener starts growing a cross-bred fruit in a converted shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' turns LEAN-TO into TANELO; G goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit, so a hybrid citrus.

clue.text: Gentle and kind, leader of government in African country

indicators.note: the first letter is placed inside the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: the leader is the front, so take the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A gentle, kindly head of government in an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kindly and harmless, the same sense as gentle and kind.

indicators.note: the first piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a group is a class or category

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outer letters of women remain

explanation.surface: An adult education class takes in some dispirited women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' means sad on the surface, but here it strips women to W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, the informal term children use.

definitions.meaning: a regiment's colours are its flag or banner

explanation.surface: Two separate words: the customary option, and a military flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or customary, and a standard is also a flag, as are a regiment's colours.

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in 'take your pick'

explanation.surface: Someone is bound by a choice that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to' reads as one phrase, but 'Subject' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion or study.

clue.text: One preparing hard for test pulls over

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tows means pulls, as a car pulls a trailer

explanation.surface: A student cramming for an exam pulls over at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for someone who studies very hard, especially before exams.

clue.text: What feller leaves behind is puzzle

definitions.meaning: a tree feller cuts down trees, leaving the stub of trunk in the ground

explanation.surface: A lumberjack's leftover is a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like 'fellow', but it is one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A stump is what remains of a felled tree, and to stump someone is to baffle them.

clue.text: Primate drawing in small recess in a church

indicators.note: the first piece draws the second inside itself

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A monkey is pictured sketching in a little church alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing in' is not sketching but taking S inside APE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded or vaulted recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

parts.note: a fluent speaker talks smoothly and easily

explanation.surface: A woman described as articulate and wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy, which is what well-to-do means.

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: firm means solid, as in firm ground

explanation.surface: A tree that is sturdy and has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir is an evergreen tree bearing cones, so a kind of conifer.

indicators.note: something on board a ship is inside it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: sooner means earlier, as in 'the sooner the better'
CH is the crossword abbreviation for check, from chess

explanation.surface: A sailor checks the board before boarding a ship earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check on board' reads as a chess move, but 'on board' signals insertion, as cargo sits inside a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing ship with two or more masts, so a kind of vessel.

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A priest who leads an Eastern church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope is head of the Roman Catholic Church, its supreme leader.
